title: Making Aldehydes and Ketones: Methods and Named Reactions
subject: Chemistry
objective: Four routes make both aldehydes and ketones (from alcohols, alkenes and alkynes); named reactions make only one: Rosenmund, Stephen, Etard and Gatterman-Koch for aldehydes; Grignard on nitriles, dialkylcadmium and Friedel-Crafts acylation for ketones.

fill.q: Oxidation of a primary alcohol gives an ____.
Rosenmund reduction uses H₂ over palladium on ____.
The Etard reaction converts toluene into ____.
Benzene and RCOCl with anhydrous AlCl₃ give an aryl ____.

tf.q: Ozonolysis of an alkene can give aldehydes, ketones or both.
tf.explain: Depends on the groups on the double-bond carbons.
Ethyne gives ethanal; other alkynes give ketones.

tf.q: The Stephen reaction goes through an imine.

ar.a: Rosenmund reduction stops at the aldehyde.
Dialkylcadmium converts an acyl chloride into a ketone.
ar.r: R′ replaces Cl on the acyl group.

short.q: How would you make acetophenone from benzene?
short.solution: Friedel-Crafts acylation: benzene + CH₃COCl with anhydrous AlCl₃ gives C₆H₅COCH₃.
